chapters.title: Historical Introduction
chapters.count_exception: Historical chapter: exercises are intentionally omitted at the user's direction.

chapters.title: Relativistic Quantum Mechanics
chapters.curation_note: Fourteen parents cover invariant one-particle normalization, the Poincare algebra and Casimirs, massive and massless little groups, discrete symmetries, finite Lorentz representations, the Bargmann cocycle, and 2+1-dimensional variants. Further fragments from the same representation-theory notes would repeat these parent derivations.

chapters.title: Scattering Theory
chapters.curation_note: Seventeen parents retain the full scattering-state, flux and phase-space, optical-theorem, Yukawa and O(N), time-ordering, partial-wave, resonance, and isospin arcs. Separate sheet problems remain separate; additional source fragments duplicate kinematic or unitarity steps already inside those parents.

chapters.title: The Cluster Decomposition Principle
chapters.curation_note: Ten complete parents naturally organize the chapter into cumulants and connected generators, locality and cluster support, the full cubic-theory vacuum-graph problem, coherent-state completeness, coherent radiation, and source additivity. The remaining candidate checks are substeps of these same five conceptual pairs.

chapters.title: Quantum Fields and Antiparticles
chapters.curation_note: Sixteen parents preserve the distinct scalar, charged-scalar, spinor, massive-vector, helicity, locality, CPT, and spin-statistics source problems. The relatively fine count is intentional because the Tong and Stanford sheets pose gamma traces, spin sums, canonical algebra, and statistics as genuinely independent complete problems.

chapters.title: The Feynman Rules
chapters.curation_note: Fifteen parents follow the actual propagator, classical-source, Wick-counting, vertex-momentum, free-Dirac, crossing, Gaussian, connected-generator, and amputation problem architecture. Assignment 4 Problem 1 and Assignment 9 Problem 2 are each kept whole; weaker one-line diagram checks were absorbed into their source parents.

chapters.title: The Canonical Formalism
chapters.curation_note: Eleven parents cover canonical transformations, improved stress tensors, the two complete MIT complex-scalar problems, constrained Hamiltonian systems, field redefinitions, and nonlinear-sigma-model geometry. The count is natural because each remaining source item is a dependent step in one of those derivations.

chapters.title: Electrodynamics
chapters.curation_note: Twelve parents span Coulomb gauge, polarization and Ward tests, scalar QED, the complete Gupta--Bleuler assignment, invariant scattering kinematics, Rutherford and electron--muon scattering, and the two Stanford electromagnetic-operator problems. Further candidates repeat phase space or split those exact parents.

chapters.title: Path-Integral Methods
chapters.curation_note: Nineteen parents retain time slicing, free kernels, oscillator and scalar sources, normalized interacting functionals, Euclidean boundaries, Pfaffians, Grassmann interactions, and one complete fermionic-Gaussian source problem. Two exact McGreevy Gaussian parents add the foundational generating-function and characteristic-function derivations; weaker determinant snippets are consolidated.

chapters.title: Non-Perturbative Methods
chapters.curation_note: Thirteen parents cover spectral positivity, scalar Ward identities and LSZ, elastic and transition form factors, subtracted dispersion relations, cut reconstruction, and low-energy and forward Compton scattering. Broad-note syntheses are retained only where no stronger standalone sheet parent covers the same nonperturbative result.

chapters.title: One-Loop Radiative Corrections in Quantum Electrodynamics
chapters.curation_note: Fourteen parents preserve the Stanford and Heidelberg one-loop integral problems, QED counterterms, Ward and four-photon tests, running and decoupling, Euler--Heisenberg matching, and the complete Pauli-form-factor derivation. Adding more items would split tensor or vertex reductions already kept intact.

chapters.title: General Renormalization Theory
chapters.curation_note: Fourteen parents cover an exact McGreevy scale-symmetry problem, operator bases and field coordinates, heavy-field matching, BPHZ and Wilsonian renormalization, classic low-energy EFTs, expansion by regions, decoupling, naturalness, unitarity, running, and fixed-accuracy predictivity. Additional broad-note prompts were weaker variants of these calculations.

chapters.title: Infrared Effects
chapters.curation_note: Twelve parents form five complete infrared arcs: eikonal soft-photon emission and real--virtual cancellation; equivalent-photon and collinear factorization; KLN-safe measurements; charged dressings and soft theorems; and soft-graviton inclusiveness. The three McGreevy parents retain their original one-, five-, and six-part boundaries, so no intermediate calculation is counted separately.

chapters.title: Bound States in External Fields
chapters.curation_note: Ten parents are the natural complete set: Pauli reduction, relativistic atomic corrections, Feynman--Hellmann and Stark problems, E1 radiation and selection rules, Uehling shifts, Green-function poles, and bound-state EFT matching. Other available items are narrower substeps or lower-quality repetitions of these calculations.
